microbenchmark.scope: Complete teacher extraction including top-k, LSE, conversions and optional row selection. Eager host wall time includes dispatch and final synchronization. Batched CUDA-graph event time amortizes host submission; neither is serving latency. No Store, D2H or Catalog work is included.

analyses.cpu_operator_attribution: Complete CPU operator events contained in a capture scope on the same process/thread. Durations are inclusive and nested calls overlap; do not sum them as wall time or treat operator events as allocation counts.
analyses.cuda_api_attribution: Complete runtime/driver API events contained in a capture scope on the same process/thread, including calls without device correlation. Nested calls may overlap; durations are CPU API time, not device work or removable wall time.

limitations: The initial 111-method suite has one stale startup fixture error, retained in the log. The corrected fixture passes separately; this is not a claim that the initial suite passed in one execution.
FlashInfer uses a pinned internal interface with per-call scratch. The actual Qwen3 profile dispatches FilteredTopKUnifiedKernel; the entry point name does not imply a radix kernel on every input.
Only nonempty CUDA FP32 vocabularies >=32768 use the optional backend. The preliminary BF16 regression is retained and BF16 stays on Torch. Defaults remain Torch.
Equal-valued boundary token IDs may differ from Torch; sorted values, unique IDs and raw gathers are exact. Full-vocabulary LSE uses the same implementation as the reference.

One Torch-then-FlashInfer off/on/off pair shows no serving throughput improvement. It is not significance or production SLO acceptance. Both use warm JIT caches, seeded producer sampling, explicit post-warmup GC freeze and the same source/instrumentation.
Profiler READY counts are not an independent content oracle. Exact online source comparison, post-exit Store readback and failure exclusion are checked by the separate runtime/P/D/serving jobs.
Kernel/API/scope durations are not additive wall-clock latency; profiler overhead is excluded from serving measurements.

Single resident H100, Qwen3-0.6B, synthetic inputs/draft weights, local TCP Store and HTTP Catalog test double. Cross-engine KV equivalence, broader models/topologies, production retention, SpecForge integration and trained quality remain unproven.
